correctness.rationale: Prime-factor divisibility forces precisely the three large prime candidates and three pure primes; the mixed candidates appear at most once, with 3^2 and 5^2 possible only for q=3 and q=5 respectively. The one q-factor source condition yields the complete exponent-budget cases a=1,2,3, and the two residual-budget exception cases are exhausted. Pairwise disjointness and all prime-dependent cardinalities follow. A standalone integer verifier independently computes all fibers for 167 odd primes q<=997 using two separate finite algorithms. No finite test is used as a proof of the unrestricted statement.

originality.rationale: He (2026), complete §5, explicitly poses s>=3 as open; Table 2 lists only finite s=3 sizes, unlike the exact all-odd-prime fiber and exception formula. Shannon et al. (2025), §2.3, treats s=2 and general enumerations but does not express the infinitely parameterized s=3 classification. Database and alias searches did not identify a stronger implication. Residual risk: unindexed older treatments of inverse totients may include the formula; this is a same-model priority assessment, not independently certified. The finite q=3,5 exception sets are already listed in the 2025 paper, and Grosswald’s 32-divisibility theorem already implies the no-singleton consequence. Novelty is asserted only for the uniform complete s=3 fiber classification and its arithmetic cardinality law.
residual_risks: An older unindexed or non-English inverse-totient paper may contain the equivalent 8q formula.
General inverse-totient enumeration algorithms produce any finite fiber after computation; the added uniform symbolic classification should not be confused with inventing that basic algorithm.
Finite search and one research database cannot certify uniqueness of discovery.
Both the two exceptional finite fibers and the no-singleton corollary are previously known; neither is included as a standalone originality contribution.

value.rationale: He (2026) explicitly poses the mirror-family classification for s>=3 as Open Problem 16. This theorem resolves the first open exponent s=3 for all odd primes, gives full solution sets and exceptional fibers, identifies a structural mod-3 split and a maximum of six generic preimages, and proves the no-singleton assertion in the whole s=3 subfamily. An exact natural classification with an open-problem motivation is substantive independently of any s>=4 extension.
